summary: The statement and proof are correct under the stated hypotheses. Refutation checks covered n=1, singleton and finite lattice supports, infinite-potential fibers, zero coordinate means, p=2, and vertical halfspaces carrying boundary mass. The moment estimates justify the weighted centroid and both entropy substitutions. The cited Melbourne-Tkocz Theorem 1.3 applies to the interval-supported coordinate laws without monotonicity; the cited 2026 Theorem 1.1 and Feige Theorem 1 both have exactly the independence, nonnegativity, mean, and strict-event hypotheses used here. Their applications give the claimed horizontal bounds. The affine shear preserves the mixed measure, and evenness of both summands justifies the paired-fiber argument for every nonvertical halfspace. The separate vertical argument and the normalization ratio yield the stated constants. No mathematical errors or gaps were found.
